quests.hint: This noun refers to a request asking someone to attend an event or occasion.
quests.explanation: 'Receive an invitation,' 'send an invitation,' and 'accept an invitation' are key collocations. 'An invitation to' is followed by a noun or verb+ing.
quests.textToSpeak: She received a lovely ___ to her friend's wedding in the countryside.
quests.correctAnswer: She received a lovely invitation to her friend's wedding in the countryside.

quests.hint: This verb means to agree to take or do something that has been offered to you.
quests.explanation: 'Accept an offer,' 'accept an invitation,' and 'accept a challenge' are key collocations. 'Accept' is more formal than 'say yes.' The noun form is 'acceptance.'
quests.textToSpeak: He was delighted to ___ the job offer after such a difficult interview process.
quests.correctAnswer: He was delighted to accept the job offer after such a difficult interview process.

quests.hint: This verb means to politely refuse something that has been offered or invited.
quests.explanation: 'Decline an invitation,' 'politely decline,' and 'decline an offer' are natural phrases. 'Decline' is more formal and polite than simply saying 'no.'
quests.textToSpeak: She had to ___ the invitation because she already had a prior commitment.
quests.correctAnswer: She had to decline the invitation because she already had a prior commitment.

quests.hint: This is a booking made in advance at a restaurant, hotel, or other venue.
quests.explanation: 'Make a reservation,' 'book a reservation,' and 'have a reservation' are key patterns. 'Reservation' is slightly more formal than 'booking' but both are used.
quests.textToSpeak: I made a ___ at the restaurant for eight o'clock on Saturday evening.
quests.correctAnswer: I made a reservation at the restaurant for eight o'clock on Saturday evening.

quests.hint: This verb means to call off or stop something that was previously arranged.
quests.explanation: 'Cancel a booking,' 'cancel a meeting,' and 'cancel a subscription' are common collocations. 'Cancellation fee' is a charge made when you cancel late.
quests.textToSpeak: We had to ___ our holiday plans because of an unexpected family emergency.
quests.correctAnswer: We had to cancel our holiday plans because of an unexpected family emergency.

quests.hint: This verb means to state that something is definitely true or will definitely happen.
quests.explanation: 'Confirm a booking,' 'confirm your attendance,' and 'please confirm' are key patterns. 'Confirmation email' is very common in modern business communication.
quests.textToSpeak: Please ___ your booking by sending an email to the address provided.
quests.correctAnswer: Please confirm your booking by sending an email to the address provided.

quests.hint: This verb means to suggest something as being good or suitable for someone.
quests.explanation: 'Recommend' takes the pattern 'recommend + noun' or 'recommend that someone do something.' 'Highly recommend' adds strong emphasis. 'Can you recommend?' is very common.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you ___ a good vegetarian restaurant near here for this evening?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you recommend a good vegetarian restaurant near here for this evening?

quests.hint: This noun is an idea or proposal offered for consideration or discussion.
quests.explanation: 'Make a suggestion,' 'have a suggestion,' and 'take a suggestion on board' are natural. 'Open to suggestions' means willing to hear ideas. 'Helpful suggestion' is common.
quests.textToSpeak: Has anyone got a ___ for a film we could all watch together tonight?
quests.correctAnswer: Has anyone got a suggestion for a film we could all watch together tonight?

quests.hint: This adjective describes something you like most of all - more than any other.
quests.explanation: 'Favourite' (British) or 'favorite' (American). 'My favourite' + noun is very common: 'my favourite restaurant,' 'my favourite song.' 'All-time favourite' adds superlative emphasis.
quests.textToSpeak: Her ___ book of all time is Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen.
quests.correctAnswer: Her favourite book of all time is Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the daily journey between your home and your place of work.
quests.explanation: 'Daily commute,' 'long commute,' and 'commute to work' are key collocations. 'Commuter train' carries commuters. 'My commute takes forty minutes' is a natural structure.
quests.textToSpeak: Her daily ___ takes about forty-five minutes each way on the underground.
quests.correctAnswer: Her daily commute takes about forty-five minutes each way on the underground.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the volume of vehicles on the roads - often causing delays.
quests.explanation: 'Heavy traffic,' 'traffic jam,' 'stuck in traffic,' and 'traffic lights' are the key collocations. 'The traffic was terrible' is one of the most common English complaints.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ on the motorway this morning was terrible and made us very late.
quests.correctAnswer: The traffic on the motorway this morning was terrible and made us very late.

quests.hint: This noun refers to how far apart two places or points are from each other.
quests.explanation: 'Walking distance' (close enough to walk). 'Distance between,' 'cover a distance,' and 'long distance' are common. 'In the distance' means far away and just visible.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ between the office and the station is only a ten-minute walk.
quests.correctAnswer: The distance between the office and the station is only a ten-minute walk.

quests.hint: This is a formal test of knowledge or ability in a subject area.
quests.explanation: 'Take an exam,' 'pass an exam,' or 'fail an exam' are the key verbs. Never 'make an exam.' 'Exam results,' 'exam preparation,' and 'mock exam' are common compounds.
quests.textToSpeak: She studied hard every evening to prepare for her final history ___.
quests.correctAnswer: She studied hard every evening to prepare for her final history exam.

quests.hint: This is a mark or score given for work completed in school or university.
quests.explanation: 'Get a good grade,' 'receive a grade,' and 'grade boundaries' are common. Letter grades (A, B, C) are used in the US; percentage grades are more common in the UK.
quests.textToSpeak: He received an excellent ___ for his essay on climate change and society.
quests.correctAnswer: He received an excellent grade for his essay on climate change and society.

quests.hint: This is a piece of school or university work given to students to complete at home.
quests.explanation: 'Do an assignment,' 'hand in an assignment,' and 'assignment deadline' are key. It is more formal than 'homework.' 'Written assignment' specifies the form.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ is due next Monday and she has not even started it yet.
quests.correctAnswer: The assignment is due next Monday and she has not even started it yet.

quests.hint: This is the two days at the end of the week - Saturday and Sunday - when most people rest.
quests.explanation: 'At the weekend' (British) or 'on the weekend' (American). 'Weekend plans,' 'this weekend,' and 'long weekend' are very common English expressions.
quests.textToSpeak: We are planning to go hiking in the mountains this ___ if the weather is good.
quests.correctAnswer: We are planning to go hiking in the mountains this weekend if the weather is good.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is calm, restful, and free from stress.
quests.explanation: 'Relaxing evening,' 'relaxing holiday,' and 'relaxing activity' are common. 'Relaxing' describes what you experience; 'relaxed' describes how you feel afterwards.
quests.textToSpeak: After a stressful week at work, all she wanted was a ___ evening at home.
quests.correctAnswer: After a stressful week at work, all she wanted was a relaxing evening at home.

quests.hint: This noun (plural) refers to arrangements or intentions for future activities.
quests.explanation: 'Make plans,' 'have plans,' and 'change plans' are the key collocations. 'Any plans?' is a very common social question. 'Plan A' and 'Plan B' are common idioms.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you have any ___ for the long bank holiday coming up next week?
quests.correctAnswer: Do you have any plans for the long bank holiday coming up next week?

quests.hint: This is a higher than normal body temperature, often a sign of infection or illness.
quests.explanation: 'Run a fever,' 'have a fever,' and 'fever breaks' (when it ends) are key collocations. 'Feverish' is the related adjective. A fever is the body's natural response to fighting infection.
quests.textToSpeak: He was running a slight ___, so the doctor advised him to rest and drink plenty of fluids.
quests.correctAnswer: He was running a slight fever, so the doctor advised him to rest and drink plenty of fluids.

quests.hint: These are the physical signs that indicate you may be ill or have a health condition.
quests.explanation: 'Have symptoms,' 'show symptoms,' and 'describe your symptoms' are the key patterns. 'Symptom' is usually used in the plural. 'Common symptoms' and 'mild symptoms' are natural.
quests.textToSpeak: She described her ___ to the doctor, including a sore throat and fatigue.
quests.correctAnswer: She described her symptoms to the doctor, including a sore throat and fatigue.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the process of getting better after illness, surgery, or injury.
quests.explanation: 'Full recovery,' 'speedy recovery,' and 'recovery time' are key collocations. 'In recovery' means currently getting better. 'Recover' is the related verb.
quests.textToSpeak: His ___ from the operation was much quicker than the doctors had expected.
quests.correctAnswer: His recovery from the operation was much quicker than the doctors had expected.

quests.hint: This is the person who serves food and drink to customers at a restaurant.
quests.explanation: 'Waiter' (male) or 'waitress' (female), though 'server' is now the preferred gender-neutral term. 'Call the waiter' or 'catch the waiter's attention' are natural.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ came to take our order and described the specials of the day.
quests.correctAnswer: The waiter came to take our order and described the specials of the day.

quests.hint: This is the document or request at the end of a meal showing the total cost.
quests.explanation: 'Ask for the bill' (British English) or 'ask for the check' (American English). 'Split the bill' means to divide the cost equally between everyone.
quests.textToSpeak: At the end of the meal, she asked the waiter to bring the ___.
quests.correctAnswer: At the end of the meal, she asked the waiter to bring the bill.

quests.hint: This is an extra amount of money given to a server for good service.
quests.explanation: 'Leave a tip,' 'give a tip,' and 'generous tip' are common expressions. Tipping customs vary widely between countries. In the UK, ten to fifteen percent is standard.
quests.textToSpeak: It is customary in many countries to leave a ___ for good service.
quests.correctAnswer: It is customary in many countries to leave a tip for good service.

quests.hint: This is a formal meeting where an employer asks questions to assess a job applicant.
quests.explanation: 'Job interview,' 'attend an interview,' 'prepare for an interview,' and 'interview questions' are key. 'The interview went well' is the standard positive outcome phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: He spent the whole evening preparing for his job ___ the following morning.
quests.correctAnswer: He spent the whole evening preparing for his job interview the following morning.

quests.hint: This is the regular payment a worker receives from their employer for their work.
quests.explanation: 'Earn a salary,' 'negotiate a salary,' and 'starting salary' are key. Salary is paid monthly; 'wages' are usually paid weekly. 'Salary slip' shows earnings breakdown.
quests.textToSpeak: She negotiated a higher ___ before she agreed to sign the employment contract.
quests.correctAnswer: She negotiated a higher salary before she agreed to sign the employment contract.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the knowledge or skill you have gained from doing something.
quests.explanation: 'Work experience,' 'years of experience,' and 'relevant experience' are key. 'Experienced' is the adjective form. 'Experience' is uncountable in this professional sense.
quests.textToSpeak: The job listing required three years of sales ___ in a similar industry.
quests.correctAnswer: The job listing required three years of sales experience in a similar industry.

quests.hint: This is a piece of written or recorded information sent to someone electronically.
quests.explanation: 'Send a message,' 'receive a message,' and 'leave a message' are key collocations. 'Text message' is informal; 'message' alone now covers all written electronic communication.
quests.textToSpeak: She sent him a quick ___ to let him know she was going to be late.
quests.correctAnswer: She sent him a quick message to let him know she was going to be late.

quests.hint: This is a recorded spoken message left when someone does not answer their phone.
quests.explanation: 'Leave a voicemail,' 'check your voicemail,' and 'listen to a voicemail' are natural. Voicemails are less common now as texting and messaging apps have taken over.
quests.textToSpeak: I missed the call but they left a detailed ___ explaining everything.
quests.correctAnswer: I missed the call but they left a detailed voicemail explaining everything.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the quality or reliability of a phone or internet signal in an area.
quests.explanation: 'Good connection,' 'poor connection,' 'lose the connection,' and 'stable connection' are key. 'WiFi connection' and 'internet connection' are very common technology collocations.
quests.textToSpeak: The call kept dropping because we had a very poor ___ in that area.
quests.correctAnswer: The call kept dropping because we had a very poor connection in that area.
